messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT OPENED — Region: us-east-1. Symptom: surge in 5xx and auth failures for Hosted API and multiple Dedicated pools. Trigger: auth-error-rate > 10% for 3m. Priority: P1 :rotating_light:

omar (oncall-sre): seeing auth failures in traces: many requests failing during token exchange with STS (assume-role calls) -> our gateway returns 502. p95 latency up ~2x. Dash: https://grafana.internal/d/abcd/us-east-auth

li (infra): aws-health shows increased error rate for STS in us-east-1 and elevated API error pages. Opening AWS support case now.

priya (runtime): runtime workers that onboard tenants are failing when fetching credentials; retries cause backlog and worker OOMs for some Dedicated pods. We're seeing large retry storms.

zane (support): fielding customer reports: "timeouts, authentication errors" from some enterprise customers. Escalating. Draft status: "We're investigating increased auth errors impacting us-east-1; engineering is working on mitigations."

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert routed to omar -> li -> priya.

omar (oncall-sre): immediate mitigations: 1) reduce token exchange frequency by enabling credential caching at gateway for 5m; 2) disable aggressive retry hooks in clients; 3) reroute new sessions away from us-east where feasible; 4) scale up warm worker pools in us-west-2 for Dedicated tenants.

li (infra): applying gateway cache change now. Config patch: ```
gateway.auth.cache_ttl: 300
gateway.auth.max_stale: 10
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: gateway-auth-cache-v2 -> env=prod -> 5 pods rolling.

priya (runtime): dropping retries on credential fetch from 5 -> 2, adding exponential backoff. Rolling to runtime pools. Command: `kubectl patch deployment runtime -p '{"spec":...}'`

li (infra): traffic steering: modifying edge routing to prefer us-west-2 for new sessions from affected IP ranges. Not forcing existing sessions to move to avoid breaking long-lived streams.

ryan (eng-sre): quick note: our observability ingest (third-party) also shows delayed logs from us-east which is making diagnosis slower. Datadog acknowledged higher ingest latency; some traces delayed up to 30s.

zane (support): posting status v1: "Investigating auth errors in us-east-1 affecting API requests and Dedicated pools. Mitigations in progress. Updates every 20 minutes."

omar (oncall-sre): handoff: li lead mitigation, I'm owning comms and post-incident.

pagerduty: omar acknowledged. Escalation to li.

li (infra): AWS support: intermittent STS 5xx in three AZs in us-east-1; they advise reducing STS call rate and implementing local caching while they remediate. ETA unknown.

priya (runtime): implemented local credential cache in runtime workers and fallback to node-local token store. Pushing config: `runtime.cred_cache.enabled=true`

li (infra): scaled Dedicated pools in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for tenants with active commitments. Initiated tenant-specific failover for tenant IDs: D-0921, D-7190. Notifying customer success.

natalie (customer-success): prepping targeted messages. Offering guided failover for affected Dedicated tenants. Will escalate to SLA team for credits if needed.

ryan (eng-sre): to avoid worker storms, we've toggled circuit-breakers on worker onboarding endpoints to 50rps per AZ. This prevents cascading retries.

priya (runtime): also disabled on-demand model prefetch for new sessions in us-east to reduce S3/metadata pressure. Will re-enable once stable.

li (infra): after cache + reduced retries + traffic steering, observed auth failures drop from 12% -> 3% over 8 minutes. Overall 5xx at 6% now.

zane (support): status v2: "Mitigations reduced error rates; some customers still impacted and receiving support. Engineering continues to monitor."

omar (oncall-sre): note: Datadog ingestion lag meant alerts arrived later — follow-up: consider multi-vendor observability fallback. Filing INT-10321.

deploy-bot: gateway-auth-cache-v2 -> deployment succeeded on 5 pods.

li (infra): AWS update: STS partial degradation persists but improving in one AZ; still recommending caching.

priya (runtime): one Dedicated tenant reported repeated errors due to sticky session to a failing worker. We've forced session migration for that tenant and restarted affected pods.

natalie (customer-success): customers notified and some accepted manual failover. Collecting impacted endpoints for postmortem.

omar (oncall-sre): mid-incident handoff: li remains primary, priya runtime lead. I'll compile timeline and own RCA. Keep pagers if >5% 5xx.

ryan (eng-sre): adding action: add token-exchange metrics + circuit-breaker dashboards to default ops view. INT-10322.

li (infra): slowly shifting a fraction of existing sessions back to us-east to test stability — no regression so far. Monitoring closely.

zane (support): prepping final customer update with mitigations and expected postmortem ETA.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — status: stabilizing. responders: li, priya, omar.

li (infra): AWS reports STS throttling alleviated in region; recommending we remove emergency caches after 2h and replace with permanent credential cache config. Will schedule follow-up change.

priya (runtime): keeping local caches for 1h then revert to normal TTLs after validation. Opening PR for configurable fallback behavior: https://git.internal/runtime/PR-2045

natalie (customer-success): post-incident outreach planned for tomorrow; customer notes captured.

omar (oncall-sre): incident summary: cause: AWS STS partial degradation in us-east-1 -> auth errors and retry storms -> elevated 5xx for Hosted API + Dedicated pools. Mitigations: edge routing, credential caching, reduced retries, circuit breakers, scaling other regions, tenant failovers. Impact: increased 5xx and auth failures for ~55 minutes peak; major tenants largely recovered via failover. Next steps: postmortem (owner: omar), infra followups (li), runtime improvements (priya), CS outreach (natalie).

pagerduty: Incident marked stable by responders.

omar (oncall-sre): moving to resolved->monitoring state. Will publish full RCA tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :bow:
